t: Find the Integer Added to Array I
o: Every element of nums1 was shifted by the same integer x to produce a multiset equal to nums2. Since a constant shift preserves order statistics, x equals min(nums2) − min(nums1) (equally, max − max, or the difference of sums divided by n). Examples: [2,6,4]→[9,7,5] gives 9−2 = 3; [10]→[5] gives −5; identical arrays give 0. Trivially O(n).
k: A constant shift maps the minimum of nums1 to the minimum of nums2.
Sorting both arrays and diffing any aligned pair also works.
The problem guarantees a valid x exists, so no verification is needed.

a.i: The shift maps extremes to extremes, so x = min(nums2) − min(nums1) in one linear pass.
s: Compute the minimum of each array.

a.i: Sorting both arrays makes the correspondence explicit; the first aligned pair differs by exactly x, which also self-verifies the guarantee.
a.sp: O(1) or O(n) depending on the sort.

w: Use the min-difference one-liner. Pitfall: none serious, but note the answer can be negative and that spread (max−min) must agree between arrays if inputs are valid. Follow-up: verify x actually transforms nums1 into nums2 (multiset check with a counter), or recover x when each element was multiplied instead of shifted.
